summary: ORBITAL ARCHITECT is an interactive space mission design simulator that transforms abstract aerospace trade-offs into hands-on systems engineering. Built around NASA’s Concept Maturity Levels (CML 1–4) and four mission segments (Launch, Space, Ground, and User), it allows solo players or teams of up to four to collaboratively design, validate, and simulate end-to-end missions. Players configure spacecraft buses, power, communications, scientific payloads, orbits, and launch vehicles while balancing budget, mass, sunlit power, eclipse battery life, and downlink bandwidth. With real-time telemetry, dynamic CAD blueprints, orbital anomaly events, and S-to-F post-mission diagnostics in English and Traditional Chinese, it helps students master real-world mission trade studies.
details:
### Overview & How It Works

ORBITAL ARCHITECT is a browser-based interactive space mission design and simulation platform created to bridge the gap between theoretical aerospace concepts and integrated systems engineering. Grounded in NASA’s four major mission segments (Launch, Space, Ground, and User) and JPL’s Concept Maturity Levels (CML 1–4) iterative workflow, the game lets learners experience how every engineering choice creates cascading trade-offs across an entire spacecraft system.

### Key Features & Gameplay Modes

- Three Play Modes & Difficulty Tiers: Supports Solo Commander, 4-Player Team Co-op (Mission Director, Spacecraft Architect, Payload Scientist, and Flight/Comms Lead—complete with inter-departmental conflict checks and joint sign-off gates), and an unconstrained Sandbox Mode across Trainee, Engineer, and Director difficulties.

- Real-Time Engineering Telemetry & Dynamic CAD Blueprint: As players configure spacecraft buses, solar arrays or MMRTG nuclear power, high-gain antennas, scientific instruments, orbits, and launch vehicles, a live SVG CAD blueprint updates dynamically alongside six coupled resource envelopes: Budget, Launch Vehicle Payload Capacity, Sunlit Power, Eclipse Battery Endurance, Daily Downlink Data Volume, and System Reliability.

- Live Orbital & Anomaly Simulation: Simulates launch ascent, orbital insertion, sunlit/eclipse power cycling, ground-station downlink passes, and dynamic in-flight anomalies (such as solar flares, low-voltage alerts, and data buffer overflows) that require real-time engineering decisions.

- Post-Mission Diagnostics & Design Iteration: Generates an S-to-F mission grade, root-cause failure/success breakdown, and side-by-side design iteration comparison table so players can refine their architecture just like NASA’s Mission Design Lab (MDL) trade studies.

- Bilingual Accessibility: Instant one-click switching between English and Traditional Chinese (繁體中文) without losing mission state.

### Tech Stack & Tools Used

- Frontend & Simulation Engine: HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), and procedural SVG rendering for real-time spacecraft CAD visualization and telemetry dashboards.

- Systems Engineering Frameworks: Modeled after NASA Systems Engineering processes, JPL Concept Maturity Levels (CML 1–4), and NASA SmallSat/CubeSat mission trade-space parameters.

### Educational Impact

By turning abstract trade-offs—such as payload mass vs. launch vehicle delta-V, instrument data rate vs. ground downlink capacity, and solar power vs. planetary eclipse duration—into immediate visual feedback, ORBITAL ARCHITECT makes real-world space mission architecture accessible and engaging for students and aspiring engineers.

### Super Intelligence (SI) Acknowledgment

Large Language Model (LLM) assistance was used to help structure the simulation physics equations, UI layout, and bilingual localization code. All system architecture, game mechanics, and NASA framework integrations were reviewed, tested, and verified by our team, and no NASA official logos or restricted mission identifiers were generated or modified.
